ownedSurfaceInventory.migrationRule: Preserve as the only formal event follow-up field family; empty string means direct close; add explicit self-reference rejection in task3.
Do not compatibility-lower. If old semantics need another authored continuation, split to explicit event + event-binding or result-local nextEventId; otherwise remove and close directly.
Retire eventStartTarget as a routing surface. Flow launch ownership must live on event.actions / event.nextEventId; returnPolicy remains playable return metadata, not a second router.

Helpers may settle effects, but must not own authored routing truth. When old helper outcomes imply a new authored continuation, split to explicit event + event-binding; if they only mean stop/return, close directly.

directClose: dialogue choice has neither nextEventId nor nextDialogueId
legacy follow-up semantics only mean stop/return with no new authored event obligation
splitToEventAndBinding: old follow-up semantics still require a new authored event after runtime/playable/navigation completion
helper-owned followUp currently triggers a domain continuation that should be event-owned
legacy dialogue/flow continuation carries a target concept outside the current event record
preserveResultLocalNextEventId: multi-result or choice result instances that already resolve through RuntimeDialogueChoiceOption.nextEventId

frozenFirstImplementationSlice.whyFirst: It enforces approved parent constraints without requiring the full routing cutover in one patch.
expectedGuards: reject explicit event.nextEventId self-reference during export/validation
keep empty nextEventId as direct close
leave broader dialogue.followUps / runtime followUp residue removal for subsequent task3 slices under the same queue
